# OTP Controller Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This specification defines the behavior of the top-level OTP controller module. The module provides controlled access to a one-time-programmable (OTP) storage array, partitions that storage into logical regions with different security and accessibility properties, protects secret data by scrambling, verifies the integrity of sensitive stored values, derives scrambling keys for other blocks, and exposes life-cycle-related state to the rest of the system.

The module is responsible for:

- Initializing and sequencing the OTP macro after power-up.
- Presenting a uniform bus and register interface to software.
- Enforcing partition-level read and write protections.
- Providing buffered and unbuffered access paths to OTP contents.
- Computing and verifying integrity digests.
- Performing periodic integrity and consistency checks.
- Scrambling and descrambling secret partitions.
- Deriving static and ephemeral scrambling keys.
- Supporting life-cycle state updates and token hashing.
- Reporting errors, interrupts, and alerts.

## 2. Reset and Startup Behavior

On reset, the module shall:

- Place all outputs in defined, inert, or invalid states.
- Keep all hardware configuration outputs invalid.
- Keep life-cycle state outputs invalid.
- Disable all access to the OTP macro.
- Clear all pending operations, interrupts, and alert state.

The module shall not access the OTP array until an external initialization request is received.

When initialization is requested, the module shall:

1. Bring the OTP macro into an operational state.
2. Power-sequence the OTP macro using the macro power-control interface.
3. Read all required partitions from the OTP.
4. Descramble secret partition data as needed.
5. Compute and verify integrity digests where required.
6. Load buffered partition contents into register storage.
7. Expose valid hardware and life-cycle outputs only after the relevant partition has initialized successfully.
8. Report initialization status in the status and error reporting interface.

If any partition fails to initialize due to an unrecoverable error, the module shall:

- Record the failure in the error-reporting registers.
- Leave the affected hardware outputs in their safe default state.
- Not expose the affected partition as valid.

The initialization-complete indication shall remain asserted once initialization has completed, until the next reset.

## 3. Logical Partitioning

The OTP storage is divided into logical partitions with the following general properties.

| Partition | Buffered | Secret | Write lockable | Software read lockable | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creator software configuration | No | No | Yes, by digest | Yes, by CSR | Calibration and configuration data |
| Owner software configuration | No | No | Yes, by digest | Yes, by CSR | Software behavior and ROM configuration |
| Hardware configuration | Yes | No | Yes, by digest | No | Hardware control and configuration bits |
| Secret 0 | Yes | Yes | Yes, by digest | Yes, by digest | Test unlock and test exit tokens |
| Secret 1 | Yes | Yes | Yes, by digest | Yes, by digest | Flash and SRAM key seeds |
| Secret 2 | Yes | Yes | Yes, by digest | Yes, by digest | RMA token and creator root key shares |
| Life cycle | Yes | No | No | No | Life-cycle state and transition counter |

### 3.1 Buffered Partitions

Buffered partition contents are read from OTP during initialization and stored in internal registers. After initialization, these buffered values are broadcast to hardware consumers.

Values programmed into a buffered partition through the programming path shall not affect live hardware outputs until the next reset or power cycle, except for the life-cycle partition, whose state output shall be updated when a life-cycle programming operation is completed.

If a buffered partition suffers an unrecoverable integrity failure, the module shall force its outputs to safe default values.

### 3.2 Unbuffered Partitions

Unbuffered partitions are read on demand. A read access to an unbuffered partition shall return OTP data through the memory-mapped access window. Such reads are subject to partition access controls.

### 3.3 Secret Partitions

Secret partitions shall be stored in scrambled form. The module shall descramble data when reading secret partitions and scramble data when writing secret partitions.

Once a secret partition has been locked by a nonzero digest:

- Software shall no longer be able to read the partition contents.
- The digest itself shall remain readable.
- The partition contents shall not be exposed through any software-accessible path.

### 3.4 Life-Cycle Partition

The life-cycle partition:

- Shall not be lockable.
- Shall not be accessible through the software direct-access interface.
- Shall be writable only through the life-cycle programming interface.
- Shall expose the current life-cycle state, transition counter, tokens, and personalization status after initialization.

## 4. Access Control

The module shall enforce the following access rules:

- A partition with a nonzero digest shall be write-locked.
- A secret partition with a nonzero digest shall also be read-locked to software.
- The creator and owner software configuration partitions may be read-locked at runtime through registers.
- The secret 2 partition shall be software-accessible only when the life-cycle provisioning qualifier is active; otherwise both read and write access shall be blocked.
- The life-cycle partition shall never be readable or writable through the software direct-access interface.
- A write attempt to a write-locked region shall be rejected with an access error.
- A read attempt to a read-locked region shall be rejected with an access error.

### 4.1 Memory-Mapped Window Accesses

Read accesses to unbuffered software configuration partitions through the memory-mapped window shall return the requested data only if the access is allowed. If the address is out of bounds, or if read access is locked, the module shall return an error response.

Write accesses through the memory-mapped window shall not be allowed.

### 4.2 Debug or Test Access

Access to the OTP macro test interface shall only be enabled when the life-cycle test-enable qualifier is active. When this qualifier is not active, no test access requests shall be issued to the OTP macro. If a test access is attempted while disabled, it shall not affect the functional state of the module.

## 5. Programming and Read Path

### 5.1 Direct-Access Interface

The direct-access interface provides software-controlled read, write, and digest-calculation commands.

A command shall only be accepted when no prior direct-access command is pending. While a command is pending, the direct-access command, address, and data registers shall be write-protected.

The direct-access interface shall support:

- 32-bit accesses for non-secret, non-digest regions.
- 64-bit accesses for secret partitions and for all digest locations.

#### Read Commands

A read command shall:

- Read from the addressed OTP location.
- Descrramble the data if the addressed partition is secret.
- Return the data through the read-data registers.
- Report an access error if the partition is read-locked.
- Report any OTP macro error through the error-reporting interface.

#### Write Commands

A write command shall:

- Write the supplied data to the addressed OTP location.
- Scramble the data if the addressed partition is secret.
- Reject the access with an error if the partition is write-locked.
- Report an error if the OTP macro detects that an already-programmed bit is being written.

#### Digest Calculation Commands

A digest-calculation command shall:

- Read the addressed partition contents.
- Compute the appropriate integrity digest.
- Write the digest to the partition-specific digest location.
- Only be accepted if the partition is still writable.
- Report an access error if the partition is write-locked.

### 5.2 Life-Cycle Programming

The life-cycle programming interface shall accept a life-cycle state transition request only after initialization has completed and no other OTP write operation is pending.

When a life-cycle state transition is requested, the module shall:

- Program the supplied life-cycle state and transition counter into the life-cycle partition.
- Preserve the ability to update previously programmed state incrementally.
- Acknowledge successful completion.
- Report an error if the OTP macro reports a failure.

A failed life-cycle programming operation shall be treated as fatal.

## 6. Partition Checks

### 6.1 Integrity Checks

Integrity checks shall verify that buffered partition contents remain consistent with their stored digests.

Integrity checks shall be performed:

- Automatically during initialization.
- Periodically, if enabled by software.
- On demand, if triggered by software.

If an integrity check fails, the module shall:

- Record a check failure.
- Trigger the fatal check alert.
- Force affected hardware outputs to safe defaults.

### 6.2 Storage Consistency Checks

Consistency checks shall verify that buffered partition contents match the current OTP storage contents.

For digest-protected partitions, the consistency check shall read the stored digest and compare it with the buffered digest.

For partitions without a stored digest, the consistency check shall read the full partition and compare it with the buffered contents.

If a consistency check fails, the module shall:

- Record a check failure.
- Trigger the fatal check alert.
- Force affected hardware outputs to safe defaults.

### 6.3 Life-Cycle Consistency Bypass

During life-cycle state updates, the life-cycle partition contents and the live life-cycle output may intentionally differ from the OTP values. The module shall bypass consistency checking for the life-cycle partition while such an update is in progress in order to prevent false failures.

### 6.4 Check Timing and Control

The module shall provide registers to:

- Enable or disable periodic integrity checks.
- Enable or disable periodic consistency checks.
- Configure a timeout for check completion.
- Trigger one-off checks.

The checks shall be disabled by default.

If a check does not complete before the configured timeout, the module shall:

- Record a timeout error.
- Trigger the fatal check alert.

### 6.5 Scrambling and Key Derivation FSM Monitoring

The module shall monitor the internal FSM state of the scrambling datapath, key derivation path, and LFSR check timer. If one of these FSMs enters an invalid state, the module shall:

- Record an FSM state error.
- Trigger the fatal check alert.
- Stop further operations from that path.

## 7. Life-Cycle Outputs

After initialization, the module shall provide:

- The current life-cycle state.
- The current life-cycle transition counter.
- The test unlock token, test exit token, and RMA token.
- The device personalization status.

The personalization status shall indicate that the device is personalized when the secret 2 partition has a nonzero digest.

The life-cycle state output shall be considered valid only when initialization of the life-cycle-relevant partitions has completed successfully.

The module shall also provide an error indication for the life-cycle partition. This indication shall reflect whether any error has been recorded in the life-cycle partition.

## 8. Key and Token Generation

### 8.1 Scrambling

The module shall scramble secret partition data using a PRESENT-based scrambling operation with a netlist-specific key. The scrambling key is a constant selected at implementation time.

Scrambling shall be transparent to users: software writes plaintext data to secret partitions, and the module scrambles it before storage. Reads return descrambled plaintext to authorized software or hardware consumers.

### 8.2 Root Key Output

The module shall provide creator root key share outputs for the key manager.

The root key output shall be valid only when the secret 2 partition has been provisioned and locked with a nonzero digest.

The key shares shall be output from the buffered secret 2 partition only when the life-cycle hardware read-enable qualifier is active. When the read-enable qualifier is not active, the module shall output safe default key values.

### 8.3 Flash Scrambling Keys

The module shall provide static flash scrambling keys derived from the flash data key seed and flash address key seed stored in secret 1.

If a flash key is requested, the module shall:

- Derive the requested key from the appropriate seed.
- Return the derived key.
- Return a seed-valid indication based on whether secret 1 has been provisioned and locked.

If the seed has not been provisioned, the module shall return a key derived from all-zero constants and shall deassert the seed-valid indication.

### 8.4 SRAM and OTBN Ephemeral Keys

The module shall provide ephemeral scrambling keys for SRAM and OTBN scrambling devices.

When an ephemeral key is requested, the module shall:

- Obtain fresh entropy from the entropy interface.
- Derive an ephemeral key from the SRAM data key seed and that entropy.
- Return the key.
- Return a nonce associated with the key.
- Return a seed-valid indication based on whether the secret 1 partition has been provisioned and locked.

If the seed has not been provisioned, the module shall return a key and nonce derived from all-zero constants and shall deassert the seed-valid indication.

The key request may remain pending while entropy is being obtained.

### 8.5 Token Hashing

The module shall provide a one-way token hashing function for life-cycle raw unlock support.

The function shall:

- Accept a raw unlock token.
- Apply a PRESENT-based one-way hash.
- Return the hashed token.

The hash shall be irreversible in practice and shall not reveal the input token.

## 9. Error Handling and Reporting

The module shall provide error-reporting registers that indicate the source and class of each error.

The error classes are:

| Error Class | Recoverable | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| No error | – | No error pending |
| OTP macro general error | No | Fatal macro alert; operation stops |
| OTP macro correctable ECC error | Yes | Reported; operation continues |
| OTP macro uncorrectable ECC error | No | Fatal macro alert; operation stops |
| OTP macro blank-write error | Yes | Reported; write is rejected |
| Access error | Yes | Reported; access is rejected |
| Check failure | No | Fatal check alert; outputs forced to defaults |
| FSM state error | No | Fatal check alert; affected path stops |

### 9.1 Error Status

The module shall expose:

- Per-partition error status.
- Check timeout status.
- Scrambling FSM error status.
- Key derivation FSM error status.
- LFSR FSM error status.
- Direct-access interface idle status.
- Background check pending status.

A newly detected monitored error condition shall generate an error interrupt event.

### 9.2 Fatal Alerts

The module shall generate two fatal alert categories:

1. Fatal macro errors, triggered by unrecoverable errors reported by the OTP macro.
2. Fatal check errors, triggered by integrity check failures, consistency check failures, check timeouts, and FSM state errors.

Fatal alerts shall remain asserted until reset.

The module shall also provide software alert-test controls that cause the alert outputs to be exercised.

### 9.3 Terminal Error State

On an unrecoverable error, the affected access path shall enter a terminal error state. In this state:

- No further commands shall be accepted from that path.
- The error indication shall remain set.
- A system reset shall be required to restore operation.

Recoverable errors shall not move the affected path into a terminal error state.

## 10. Interrupt Behavior

The module shall provide two interrupts:

1. Operation-done interrupt, asserted when a direct-access operation completes successfully or with an error.
2. Error interrupt, asserted when a new error condition is recorded.

Both interrupts shall be maskable and shall have associated interrupt-test capabilities.

## 11. Power and Idle Behavior

The module shall provide an idle indication that tells the power controller whether it is safe to power down the OTP.

The idle indication shall be deasserted while:

- A direct-access write or digest operation is in progress.
- A life-cycle programming operation is in progress.

When no programming operation is pending, the idle indication shall be asserted.

The module shall not be considered idle during initialization.

## 12. Entropy Interface

The module shall use the entropy interface for two purposes:

- Reseeding the LFSR-based check timer.
- Supplying fresh entropy for ephemeral key derivation.

If entropy is not available, the module shall keep the requesting operation pending until entropy is provided.

## 13. Implementation-Specific Configuration

The module shall be configurable with:

- A netlist-specific LFSR seed and permutation.
- Netlist-specific scrambling keys for secret partitions.
- Netlist-specific digest initialization vectors and finalization constants.
- A netlist-specific raw unlock token constant.
- An optional OTP memory initialization image.

These constants shall be fixed at implementation time and shall be used consistently by all scrambling, digest, and key-derivation operations.
